resources.string: Mark the start of your period and your cycle will appear here.
Many people notice in this phase
The phases of your cycle; the mark shows today
Approximate levels of estrogen, progesterone, LH, FSH and testosterone across the cycle
The curves are a typical model stretched to your cycle length. They are not test results: real levels differ from person to person.
Estrogen (estradiol) rises in the first half of the cycle: it thickens the uterine lining and affects mood, energy and skin.
Progesterone is produced after ovulation: it prepares the uterine lining, slightly raises body temperature and makes many people calmer and sleepier.
Luteinizing hormone (LH) surges just before ovulation, and that surge releases the egg. Ovulation tests detect it.
Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) helps follicles mature early in the cycle and also rises a little at ovulation.
Small amounts of testosterone are normal; around ovulation many people link it to higher libido and confidence.
Low, so energy may be lower than usual.

Near its peak, often a time of energy and sociability.
A second, smaller rise, falling towards the end of the phase.
Starts to rise after the egg is released.
The main hormone of this phase: sleepiness, appetite and tender breasts are possible.
Still low; it peaks just before ovulation.
LH surge: an ovulation test may be positive these days.
